items.s: India's first Super computer to be counted among the world's top 500 computers
items.x:
Exam key: PARAM Siddhi-AI (India's top TOP500 entry in 2020). Strictly: PARAM Padma was the first Indian system on the TOP500, June 2003, rank 171 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercomputing_in_India via web search).
Exam key: PARAM Siddhi-AI, which entered the TOP500 at rank 62/63 (Nov 2020) and was India's highest-ranked system then. Strictly, the first Indian system in the TOP500 was PARAM Padma (June 2003, rank 171); PARAM 8000 and 10000 never entered it.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
items.s: As of July 2022, what is India's radiation exposure limit for mobile towers?
items.x:
Official key: 9.2 watt/m². Strictly: India's limit is 1/10th of ICNIRP – about 0.9 W/m² at 1800 MHz (0.45 at 900 MHz); 9.2 is the ICNIRP figure (DoT presentation, ITU 2013).
Official key: 9.2 W/m². India's limits (from 1 Sept 2012) are one-tenth of ICNIRP – 0.45 W/m² at 900 MHz and 0.90 W/m² at 1800 MHz; 9.0-9.2 W/m² is the ICNIRP level at 1800 MHz. (Moved to telecom.)

items.s: Which of the following is not used as rocket propellant –
items.x:
Printed key: (b) liquid oxygen. Strictly: all four are used; LOX is a propellant component (oxidiser) (NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.10-11; PMF S&T Part 1 p.137).
The printed key takes liquid oxygen as 'not a propellant' because it is the oxidiser, not a fuel. In fact LH2, LOX, hydrazine and kerosene (RP-1) all serve as rocket propellants.

items.s: Which of the following is NASA's first Human Mission to the Lunar south Pole to commence in 2025?
items.x:
NASA restructured Artemis in Feb 2026 — now Artemis III is a 2027 low-Earth-orbit lander test and Artemis IV (2028) the first crewed landing (Rocket CA 2026 Part 2 p.94)
Artemis III was announced as NASA's first crewed landing near the lunar south pole (then 2025); Pioneer 1-3 were 1958 probes. In 2026 NASA made Artemis III a 2027 Earth-orbit test, and the landing moved to Artemis IV (2028) (now Artemis IV).

items.s: Agni-III, the missile which was test fired in February, 2010 has the longest range of:
items.x:
Official key / most-told answer for this PYQ: 3,700 km. Strictly: most notes give Agni-III about 3,500 km (NextGen S&T Part 2 p.57; PMF S&T Part 6 p.64: 3,000-3,500 km).
The key marks 3,700 km for the Agni-III tested on 7 February 2010; Agni-III is usually given as about 3,500 km (NextGen) or 3,000-3,500 km (PMF), with reported maximum ranges above 3,500 km.

items.s: Which was the third country in the world to hold S-400 missiles after Russia and Belarus?
items.x: China was the first foreign buyer of the Russian S-400 (contract 2014-15, deliveries from 2018); Turkey and India followed. The printed key is kept, though Belarus's own S-400 holding is poorly documented.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
items.s: Which of the following radioactive elements is used in cancer therapy?
items.x:
Printed key: Cobalt-62 (misprint). Strictly: Cobalt-60 is the cancer-therapy isotope (PMF S&T Part 4 p.31).
Key A: the paper's 'Cobalt-62' is a misprint for Cobalt-60, whose gamma rays are used in cancer radiotherapy; U-235, Pu and Th-233 are reactor fuels, not therapy isotopes.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: What is the goal of PM Surya Ghar Yojana?
o: Install rooftop solar panels in urban areas
items.x: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024, MNRE) installs rooftop solar on residential houses, aiming at 1 crore homes and up to 300 free units a month. It covers rural homes too, but rooftop solar is the only fitting option.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: As per which amendments of Montreal Protocol, India will reduce the use of HFCS by 85 per cent over the 2024-26 baseline by 2045.
items.x: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol phases down HFCs. India (Group 2) has a 2024-26 baseline, freezes in 2028 and cuts 85% by 2047 (the stem's 2045 is the Group 1 date).

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
items.s: According to an estimate made in 2016 by the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India, how much bio-medical waste is generated annually in India?
items.x:
Official key / most books: 17 lakh tonnes. Strictly: MoEF (2016) gave 0.17 million tonnes = 1.7 lakh tonnes a year (Shankar Environment Part 7 p.8; DownToEarth on SWM Rules 2016).
MoEF's 2016 figure was 0.17 million tonnes of biomedical waste a year (about 1.7 lakh tonnes). The key reads it as 17 lakh, and 15 lakh is the e-waste figure from the same release.
